column7: "planExcerpt": "# Phase 2: Full Browser Mode Migration Plan\\n\\n## Goal and scope\\n\\nMove the original 89 partial candidate scenarios (the disjoint prior-51 and B3m-38 rosters) to full Vitest Browser Mode ownership, reaching `partial=0`. The target stack is Vitest and `@vitest/browser-playwright` 4.1.11 with Playwright 1.62.1. The frozen [89-row audit crosswalk](full-migration-roster.md) records stable IDs, source predicates, Browser Mode owners, remaining work, classification, and batch assignment.\\n\\nViewport, DOM/layout, hover, keyboard/focus, wheel/scroll, Chromium/WebKit, and touch emulation are supported or achievable with setup. Current component fixtures do not establish production Next route or server-data coverage; this is an unproven integration boundary, not evidence of technical impossibility.\\n\\n## Staged execution\\n\\n1. **Freeze and reconcile the ledger before implementation.** The frozen roster has exactly 89 unique IDs in sequential 20/20/20/20/9 batches. Counts are prior-51 A=0/B=44/C=7, B3m-38 A=0/B=36/C=2, total A=0/B=80/C=9. These are the original partial candidates, not proof that all 89 have a live unmigrated predicate. Resolve every C source predicate and any flagged source mismatch before implementation. Never mark a row complete merely because an E2E assertion was deleted; confirm a current source predicate and its complete Browser Mode owner, or correct the ledger status if the predicate was already transferred or no longer exists.\\n2. **Prove the production-route path.** The [Next.js 16 Vitest guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/16/app/guides/testing/vitest) says async Server Components are unsupported through the standard Next Vitest integration; this constraint is distinct from browser APIs. Spike a Playwright-provider custom command with browser context/new-page access and a Next server harness. Build a minimal production Next route PoC that a Browser Mode test can operate and observe, including its route URL, server-provided data, and a visible chart/result predicate. Verify the exact APIs against the installed versions. If the first approach is blocked, isolate the limitation and try the minimum supported context/page and server-harness alternatives. Do not mark scenarios unsupported without reproducible technical evidence and JEV review.\\n   Before writing or changing Next.js code for the PoC or harness, read the applicable version guide under `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` as required by the repository's `AGENTS.md`.\\n3. **Reconcile source status and known mappings.** A means a live predicate reproducible by component fixtures alone; B means a live predicate requiring route/data/build/page-context integration; C means source predicate ownership/mapping is deleted, transferred, or unresolved, not technical unsupported. The roster flags acceptance-187 as P42-193..201 and readability-191 as P42-219..240; the earlier attribution of P42-223..231 to acceptance-187 was wrong. Keep those predicates at their respective source callsites until reconciled. Row201 (`p45-b-mobile-ux-201-lazymount-p5-1`) is in prior-51; production P42-349/-350 remain route E2E and P42-351 is unit-owned. Resolve its ledger wording before changing status.\\n4. **Migrate in five batches.** Use batches of 20, 20, 20, 20, and 9 stable IDs, following the reconciled inventory order. For every ID, establish assertion parity first, then remove only its corresponding E2E predicate after the Browser Mode equivalent passes. Run the retained E2E regression after each 20-row batch and after the final batch. Keep unrelated E2E checks. Batch reports must list IDs, source-to-target predicate mapping, fidelity evidence, removed assertions, focused results, E2E result, and remaining gaps.\\n5. **Close the ledger.** Audit all 89 IDs for exactly-once accounting, source-assertion ownership, test evidence, and E2E removals. An unresolved source mapping remains an explicit tracked item; it must not be silently treated as either a technical exclusion or a completed transfer.\\n\\n## Fidelity and parity requirements\\n\\nFor each scenario, preserve the source predicate and its meaningful inputs. The coverage map must state whether data comes from the real production route/server path or a fixture, and identify the route/build/page-shell boundary; viewport and layout dimensions; pointer, keyboard, focus, wheel, or touch interaction; and Chromium or WebKit engine. Use production route/data coverage wherever the source assertion depends on it. A component fixture is sufficient only where it reproduces the complete source predicate without a production integration dependency. Do not weaken thresholds, selected values, output expectations, page-error checks, or interaction assertions to make migration pass.\\n\\n## Gates, risks, and decisions\\n\\n- The route PoC is the first decision gate. A failure should produce a minimal reproducer and a tested next supported path (for example, provider custom command/context lifecycle or server startup/teardown adjustment). Escalate a claimed technical boundary with exact evidence and JEV review before changing scenario eligibility.\\n- C-row reconciliation is a ledger/source-mapping gate, not a browser-capability gate. Keep any missing source assertion visible until its owner and disposition are established.\\n- At each batch gate, compare the Browser Mode predicate and the E2E predicate side by side before deletion. Failed parity or E2E regression blocks that batch’s removals; unrelated assertions remain intact.\\n- Browser engine, viewport, touch, and production-data fidelity can vary by row. Run the row in every engine/input context required by its source contract; do not infer WebKit or touch coverage from Chromium mouse coverage.\\n\\n## Acceptance and reporting\\n\\nAccept Phase 2 when the original 89-row candidate roster has been reconciled; each live source predicate has a passing, complete Browser Mode owner or an auditable ledger correction; no row is marked complete solely because an E2E assertion disappeared; the eligible roster has `partial=0`; all five retained E2E batch gates pass; and no unrelated E2E assertion was removed or weakened. Report per-batch counts/results, source-to-test crosswalk, C-row dispositions, route-PoC evidence, limitations with JEV outcome, and final inventory totals.\\n\\n## Capability references\\n\\nOfficial references for the spike and per-row evidence: [Vitest Browser Mode](https://vitest.dev/guide/browser/), [Vitest browser viewport](https://vitest.dev/config/browser/viewport.html), [browser interactivity](https://vitest.dev/config/browser/interactivity), [custom browser commands](https://vitest.dev/api/browser/commands), [Playwright provider](https://vitest.dev/config/browser/playwright), [Playwright BrowserContext](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext), [Playwright page](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page), and [Playwright emulation](https://playwright.dev/docs/emulation). Confirm exact behavior against the pinned project versions during the PoC.\\n",
